Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILGNAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City MR. MARIANO GABITO Bik. 1, Lot 2, Phase I-A http: //www.dilg.com.ph 01 AUG OILG OPINION NO. 41 s. 2019. Dalton Street, Brgy. San Manuel City of San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan Dear Mr. Gabito: This has reference to your letter dated 11 November 2018 requesting for this Department's position on whether or not a former three-termer Municipal Mayor who failed to clear himself from his accountabilities as local chief executive at the end of his term, can still qualify as an official candidate for this coming 2019 Local Elections, for the same position in the Municipality of Sabtang, Batanes. Foremost, Sections 39 and 40 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code" (LGC) provides for the qualifications and disqualifications for an elective local officials, to wit: "SECTION 39. Qualifications. - (a) An elective local official must be a citizen of the Philippines; a registered voter in the Barangay, municipality, city, or province or, in the case Ofa member of the Sangguniang Pamala wigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, or Sanggunian bayan, the district where he intends to be elected; a resident therein for at least one (I) year immediately preceding the day of the election; and able to read and write Filipino or any other local language or dialect. xxx (c) Candidates for the position of Mayor or vice-mayor of independent component cities, component cities, municipalities must be at least twenty-one (21) years of age on election day. .xxx SECTION 40. Disqualifications. - The following persons are disqualified from running for any elective local position:

(a) Those sentenced by finaljudgment for an offense involving moral turpitude or for an offense punishable by one (l) year or more Of imprisonment, within two (2) years after serving sentence; (b) Those removed from office as a result dan administrative case; (c) Those convicted by final judgment for violating the oath of allegiance to the Republic; (d) Those with dual citizenship; (e) Fugitives from justice in criminal or nonpolitical cases here or a broad; (f) Permanent residents in a foreign country or those who have acquired the right to reside abroad and continue to avail of the same right after the effectivity of this Code; and (g) The insane or feeble-minded. " On the bases of the afore-quoted provisions of law, inasmuch as a person possesses the qualifications and none of the disqualifications, such person may run for an elective local position. The prohibition on the three-term limit rule does not apply to the herein Municipal Mayor as his Mayoralty candidacy for the 2019 Local Elections is not within the prohibition as contemplated in Section 8, Article X of the Constitution and Section 43(b) of the LGC, that, except for barangay officials, no local elective official shall serve for more than three (3) consecutive terms in the same position. Per your letter, the Municipal Mayor, after his three (3) consecutive terms from 2007-2016, ran and won as Member of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in the Province of Batanes last 2016 Local Elections. Thus, his membership to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan is an interruption to his three consecutive term. Accordingly, the three-term limit rule is no longer applicable to his candidacy for Mayoralty this coming 2019 Local elections as the prohibition pertains to three consecutive terms. With respect to your question on what happens to his previous accountabilities if he wins, we find the question too vague and general as there is/are no specific acts/omissions committed by the said Mayor. Nevertheless, please be guided that Article 218 of the Revised Penal Code provides that: "ARTICLE 218. Failure of Accountable Officer to Render Accounts. — Any public officer, whether in the service or separated therefrom by resignation or any other cause, who is required by law or

regulation to renderaccount to the InsularAuditor, or to aprovincial auditor and who fails to do so for a period of two months after such accounts should be rendered, shall be punished by prisiön correccional in its minimum period, or by a fine ranging from 200 to 6, 000 pesos, or both. " Hence, assuming that he wins this 2019 Elections, and provided that the allegations against the Mayor are true, the above-mentioned provision of the law is very clear that the latter can still be held liable for Failure of Accountable Officer to Render Accounts. Moreover, in support to the above-mentioned law, the Department issued Memorandum Circular No. 2019-39, dated 13 March 2019, requiring the Provincial Governors and City/Municipal Mayors to create a Local Governance Transition Team in their respective local government units (LGUs) for purposes of ensuring the smooth local governance transition to the newly-elected or re-elected local officials, with the following tasks and responsibilities: a. b. C. d. e. Conduct an inventory on LGU properties; Gather, secure, and preserve all official documents and/or records Of LGU official transactions; Turnover accountabilities using the prescribed forms; Organize a turnover ceremony; and Ensure the accomplishment and timely submission of Elective Local Offcial Personnel Data Sheet (ELOPDS) by the incoming officials. Non-compliance with the said Memorandum Circular will be dealt with in accordance with applicable laws and other pertinent issuances. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: MARIVEL C. S NCILLO, CESO 111 U dersecretary CC: Dir. J ulie J. Daquioag Regional Director DILG-Region 111
